purpose: Freeze the exact Campaign120 dictionary-phrase mechanism and challenge it against every nearby terminal family before any source row or value is read.

candidate.name: intraday_return_direction_dictionary_phrase_count_238s
candidate.selected_bar_grid: Exactly 240 raw unadjusted one-minute closes at 09:31-11:30 and 13:01-15:00; preserve but exclude standalone 09:30.
candidate.direction_sequence: Inside each 120-close half form exactly 119 symbols: -1 when close_t<close_t-1, 0 on exact numeric equality, and +1 when close_t>close_t-1. Do not form a lunch or overnight symbol.
parser: Reset an empty phrase dictionary and cursor i=0 at the start of each 119-symbol half.
At cursor i, find the longest nonempty prefix w of the remaining suffix that is already an exact dictionary member; when no member matches, w is the empty word.
If at least one symbol remains after w, emit phrase w followed by that next symbol, add the emitted phrase to the dictionary, advance past it, and increment the phrase count by one.
If w consumes the entire remaining suffix, emit that reused suffix once as the terminal phrase, do not add it again, increment the phrase count by one, and stop.
Continue until all 119 symbols are consumed. Sum morning and afternoon phrase counts; dictionaries never cross lunch, session, stock or date.
candidate.normalization: none because both sequences have the same frozen length 119
candidate.validity: All 240 closes must be finite and strictly positive; every symbol and phrase must be consumed exactly once under the frozen parser; the result must be a finite integer in [2,238]. Constant and partially unchanged paths are valid.
candidate.economic_hypothesis: Higher incremental phrase novelty represents a wider completed-session repertoire of direction motifs and less dominance by stale or mechanically repeating micro-paths, potentially indicating more resilient information absorption over the next three sessions.

overlap_challenges.reason: The terminal factor retains only the imbalance of adjacent ++ versus -- counts and includes the lunch return. Campaign120 resets at lunch and parses every -1/0/+1 symbol into variable-length dictionary phrases. Synthetic sequences (-1,-1,-1,-1,-1,-1,0,-1) and (-1,-1,-1,-1,-1,0,-1,-1) have identical marginal and adjacent-pair counts but frozen parser counts 5 and 4.

Bar-direction continuity reads open-close body signs and collapses them to one informative-pair continuation rate with a 120-pair support threshold. Campaign120 reads no open, has no threshold, retains zeros as symbols and preserves longer phrase recurrence.

Weak-order entropy classifies overlapping triples by the relative magnitudes of three returns and discards all ordering beyond its pooled 13-state histogram. Campaign120 is invariant to magnitude changes that preserve direction symbols and retains variable-length chronological phrase recurrence; residual empirical redundancy must still pass the strict numeric gate.

Spectral entropy uses demeaned signed return magnitudes and distributes Fourier power across 59 frequencies. Campaign120 uses no magnitude, mean, Fourier coefficient or entropy and is a discrete dictionary parsing statistic.

Clock entropy retains only ten time-bin counts of exact close changes and discards direction and within-bin order. Holding every update location fixed while changing its direction motifs can change Campaign120 without changing clock entropy.
Exact-level diversity is invariant to a permutation of the 240 close multiset and uses no clock order. Such a permutation can change Campaign120's symbol sequence and phrase parsing.
Campaign120 reads no amount or volume and imposes no active-trading predicate; activity may be empirically associated with phrase novelty but is not part of its definition.

Campaign119 uses high and low joint boundary changes and a pooled nine-state histogram. Campaign120 reads close only and parses ordered ternary close-direction phrases; it does not transition or reparse Campaign119 states.

frozen_counterfactuals: Changing return magnitudes without changing exact close-direction symbols leaves Campaign120 unchanged but can change return weak-order and spectral entropy.
Keeping the ternary marginal and adjacent-pair counts fixed can still change Campaign120 because phrase discovery depends on longer chronological context.
Permuting the same exact close-level multiset can change Campaign120 while leaving exact-close-level diversity unchanged.
Changing amount, volume, high, low or open while preserving all selected closes leaves Campaign120 unchanged.
rejected_variants_before_values: LZ76, LZ77, compressor byte length, suffix-tree, grammar, Kolmogorov proxy or another parser
